errors.problem: the Arabic is correct (article + hamzat waṣl word, kasra carried by the lām) but the engine renders it 'Iliāstifhām', 'Iliāsmiyya', 'Iliāstiʿlāmāt' — the article is split into 'Ili' + 'ā' and the learner sees an unreadable transliteration on every tap of these three grammar terms
errors.fix: engine: when alif-lām with a kasra on the lām is followed by a bare alif + sukūn letter, elide the alif and output al-istifhām, al-ismiyya, al-istiʿlāmāt
errors.alsoChange: check any other key or seg whose article precedes a hamzat-waṣl word (الِانْتِقَال, الِابْن …)

errors.problem: أَحَد is a real, common word: 'one, someone, anyone' (لَا أَحَد, أَحَدُ الطُّلَّاب, and the 'one' in eleven). Because the hand glossary overrides every gloss, a learner tapping أَحَد anywhere in the course is told it is a wrong form of Sunday
errors.fix: أَحَد = one, someone, anyone (Sunday is al-aḥad, with 'the')
errors.alsoChange: keep the 'wrong — correct' remark in the mistakes pair's own note, not in the glossary

errors.current: ـُوا = you all (ending of an order to a group: -ū)
errors.problem: ـُوا is first of all the past-tense 'they' ending (زَرَعُوا, حَصَدُوا, نَجَحُوا, ذَهَبُوا — all in this course) and the 'they / you all' ending after أَنْ, لَمْ, لَا; glossing it only as the imperative 'you all' tells the learner زَرَعُوا is an order
errors.fix: ـُوا = -ū (ending: they, in the past tense; you all, in an order or after an / lam)

errors.current: تُعْطِي = you give (to a woman); she gives
errors.problem: indicative تُعْطِي is 2nd person masculine ('you give, to a man') or 3rd feminine ('she gives'); 'you give (to a woman)' is تُعْطِينَ (the nūn-less تُعْطِي for a woman exists only after lā / lam / an). Same pattern as the correct entries تُقَابِلُ and تَرُدُّ
errors.fix: تُعْطِي = you give (to a man); she gives

errors.problem: صِينِيَّة is also the everyday feminine nisba 'Chinese (f)' (هِيَ صِينِيَّة), a form a nationality lesson is likely to use; the hand glossary overrides every seg, so a learner tapping it in a nationality sentence gets 'tray'

errors.path: جُمُعَة; بَارِدُونَ; طَبَقَانِ; يَزُورُونَ; أَجِدُهَا; أَجْلِسُ; جَوَازِي; تُوقِظُنَا; الْأَشْهَرُ; الْأَخْبَارِ; إِنْتَرْنِت; الْمِفْتَاحُ; زَرَعُوا; حَصَدُوا; تَذْكِرَتَانِ; بَنَتِ; الْفَائِقِ; الضَّجِيجُ; الطَّرِيقُ; نَجَحُوا; أُعْلِنَ; غَائِمَاتٌ; غَائِمِينَ; أُسَجِّلُ
errors.current: طَبَقَانِ = two dishes (wrong after a verb — correct: ṭabaqayni)
errors.problem: these 24 keys are all correct Arabic forms in their own right (طَبَقَانِ as a subject, الضَّجِيجُ as a subject, الْأَخْبَارِ after a preposition, زَرَعُوا with a pronoun subject, أَجْلِسُ as plain indicative, جَوَازِي 'my passport/permit', etc.), but the gloss carries a one-sentence remark 'wrong here / wrong after …'. Because the hand glossary wins app-wide, the remark appears wherever the word is tapped, including sentences where the form is right. (The misspelt or non-existent keys such as غُرْفَةُهُ, زَارْنَا, أَفْضَلَة, أُمْكِنُ are fine: they cannot occur correctly.)
errors.fix: keep only the dictionary gloss (e.g. 'two dishes (subject form)', 'the noise', 'they sowed', 'I sit', 'my passport', 'the news (genitive)', 'cloudy (f pl)') and move the 'wrong — correct …' remark to the mistakes item's own explanation field
errors.alsoChange: for طَبَقَانِ and تَذْكِرَتَانِ the rule text is also inexact: the -ayni form is required when the dual is the object or after a preposition, not simply 'after a verb' (a subject can follow its verb: جَاءَ طَبَقَانِ)

errors.current: ـَيْنِ = -ayni (dual ending after a verb or preposition)
errors.problem: 'after a verb' is not the rule: the subject also follows its verb in Arabic (جَاءَ كِتَابَانِ is correct). The -ayni / -īna forms are the object (accusative) and after-preposition (genitive) forms
errors.fix: ـَيْنِ = -ayni (dual ending for the object of a verb, or after a preposition); same wording for ـِينَ and كِتَابَيْنِ ('two books, as object or after a preposition')

errors.problem: the possessive endings -hā and -hu are also 'its' (اِسْمُهَا of a city, بَابُهُ of a house); the object-ending entries ـهَا / ـهُ correctly say 'her, it' but the possessive ones only say 'her' / 'his'
errors.fix: ـُهَا = her, its (ending: -hā); ـُهُ = his, its (ending: -hu)

errors.problem: تَأْمِين means 'insurance, securing'; the 'security deposit' sense is a narrower everyday use (and the course has عُرْبُون = deposit separately). As an app-wide gloss 'deposit' alone would mislabel تَأْمِين صِحِّيّ / تَأْمِين السَّيَّارَة
سَمَحْتُمْ is past tense ('you allowed / permitted'); the present gloss hides the form, and the idiom the learner meets is لَوْ سَمَحْتُمْ = 'please (if you would allow)'
errors.fix: سَمَحْتُمْ = you allowed, you permitted (to several people; law samaḥtum = please)

errors.problem: subjunctive تُسَاعِدَ is 'you help (to a man)' or 'she helps'; the entry gives only the 2nd person and omits the gender restriction that sister entries (تُقَابِلُ, تَرُدُّ) state
errors.fix: تُسَاعِدَ = you help (to a man); she helps (form after an)

errors.current: لِلْمَسْجِدِ = the mosque has (lit. to the mosque)
errors.problem: a sentence meaning ('the mosque has') is given as the word gloss; لِلْمَسْجِدِ is simply 'to / for the mosque' and only means 'has' when it is the predicate of a nominal sentence
errors.fix: لِلْمَسْجِدِ = to the mosque, for the mosque (as predicate: the mosque has)

errors.problem: الْعَدَّاد is any meter / counter (electricity meter, speedometer); 'taxi' is the context of one dialogue, not part of the word
errors.fix: الْعَدَّاد = the meter (counter; in a taxi: the fare meter)

errors.problem: transliteration 'Ashalu' merges s + h into the digraph sh, so the word reads as *ashalu; likewise 'Yadhhabūna' / 'Tadhhabīna' put dh + h side by side. ALA-LC separates such clusters with a prime (as′halu, yadh′habūna)
errors.fix: engine: insert a separator (′ or ·) between s-h, d-h, t-h, k-h, g-h when the two letters are separate consonants: as′halu, yadh′habūna, tadh′habīna

notes.note: unvocalised keys transliterate as consonant skeletons ('Nt', 'Mṭbkh', 'Rʾīnā'); if the transliteration is shown for these keys, either vocalise them (أَنْتَ/أَنْتِ, مَطْبَخ, رَأَيْنَا) or suppress the ⟶ line for unvocalised keys. The أنت gloss itself is good.
'(taught in week 5)' is course meta-information shown on every tap of لَيْسَ, including in week 5 and after; consider dropping it from the gloss.

glossed only as the grammar term 'the predicate (lit. the news)'; if a reading text ever uses الْخَبَر in its plain sense 'the news item', this override will show the grammar term. Fine as long as the word appears only in grammar pages.
'my (ending: -ī)' is right for nouns; the same shape is the feminine 'you' ending of imperatives (صَوِّرِي, اِضْغَطِي). Only a problem if the segmenter splits verb endings with this key.
'the condition, things' — 'things' only fits كَيْفَ الْحَال; 'the state, the condition (how things are)' reads more clearly.
glossed as the grammar term 'adverbs'; the everyday meanings 'circumstances' and 'envelopes' will be hidden if the word appears in a dialogue.
the remark 'standard Arabic: ʿaṭshā / ghaḍbā' is accurate (فَعْلَان → فَعْلَى); عَطْشَانَة is widely accepted in modern MSA too, so the entries are fine.
the correction text 'lil-ṭabbākhīna' is not assimilated like the house style elsewhere ('li-ṭ-ṭabbākhīna'); cosmetic.
'piaster (1/100 of a dinar)' is right for Jordan; it is also 1/100 of the Egyptian/Syrian/Lebanese pound. Consider '1/100 of a dinar or pound'.
'Sun' and 'Rise' as parts of a hotel name are fine as long as no other content uses سَن (tooth/age, usually سِنّ) or رَايْز.
شَحَنَ also 'shipped, loaded'; حَمَّلَ also 'loaded, uploaded'. The phone-context glosses are correct for the course.
all Levantine Gregorian month names, all Hijri month names, the numeral-gender notes (سِتُّ, ثَلَاثُ, أَحَدَ, اِثْنَا) and the ordinal/time entries checked and correct.

summary: Read all 409 hand-glossary entries as app-wide dictionary glosses and checked each transliteration against its harakat. 14 errors: 5 major (engine renders the article before hamzat-waṣl words as 'Iliā…' in 3 keys; أَحَد glossed only as a 'wrong' Sunday although it means 'one/someone'; ـُوا glossed only as the imperative 'you all' although it is the past 'they' ending in this course; تُعْطِي glossed as 'you (to a woman)' instead of 'you (to a man)/she'; صِينِيَّة 'tray' hides 'Chinese (f)') and 9 minor (24 valid forms carrying one-sentence 'wrong — correct' remarks, grouped; 'after a verb' as the rule for -ayni/-īna; -hā/-hu missing 'its'; تَأْمِين, سَمَحْتُمْ, تُسَاعِدَ, لِلْمَسْجِدِ, الْعَدَّاد narrowed or shifted; s-h/dh-h digraph ambiguity in the engine). The main pattern: the file mixes true dictionary glosses with mistakes-pair commentary ('wrong here', 'wrong after inna'), which is harmless on non-words but leaks onto correct forms wherever they occur. Vocabulary glosses, month names, number-gender rules, pronoun endings and grammar-term entries are otherwise accurate; 12 notes for the owner.
